paper_design_summary: In two Prolific experiments and one university laboratory experiment, participants were randomly assigned to an LLM summary or a real/simulated web-link learning condition, then wrote advice that was scored for similarity across writers, length, and factual references. Experiment 2 used GPT-4o-generated content in both presentation conditions. A separate recipient experiment rated the Experiment 3 texts; three supplementary replications are described only briefly in the saved article.

outcomes.name: Recipient-rated helpfulness of advice, with side-by-side choice as a convergent variant (Experiment 4)
outcomes.measure_detail: Independent MTurk Connect recipients, blind to source condition, rated one randomly drawn text from each Experiment 3 condition in randomized order. Main item: I find this advice very helpful, agreement 1-5; repeated-measures ANOVA. The same recipients then chose which of the two texts was more helpful, with a tie option; chi-square test. Both formats are grouped as helpfulness. The main observation is one recipient rating of one text; side-by-side choice compares a pair of texts, with one paired judgment per recipient (p. 8, Method and Results). There were 1,493 analyzed recipients (p. 8). Precision is based on recipient responses; the article does not report adjustment for reuse of the same writer texts.
outcomes.delay: Advice was produced in Experiment 3 immediately after search; assessed later by separate Experiment 4 recipients. Elapsed time to rating is not stated, and AI availability during production is unresolved.

eligibility.reason: Experiments 1-3 randomly assigned people to an LLM learning aid or an alternative presentation before writing advice (pp. 3, 6, 7, Methods). They analyzed 1,104, 1,979, and 250 writers, respectively, each independently exceeding 50 people (same passages). Advice texts were scored for diversity across writers using pairwise cosine similarity and Levenshtein distance (p. 4, text-analysis methods; pp. 5-7, Results), qualifying under the codebook rule admitting writing tasks compared across writers for similarity. Experiments 1 and 3 compare generative AI with web search (ai_vs_active); Experiment 2 supplies GPT-4o-generated content in both formats (ai_design; p. 6, Methods). Recipient recommendation and adoption intentions are ancillary and do not satisfy criterion 3; removing their eligibility contribution leaves the diversity evidence intact. Core eligibility does not depend on whether AI remained available during writing; that unresolved detail determines after_ai versus with_ai/across_people classification. S4 recipients do not count toward writer samples. Missing details may affect eligibility of supplementary studies individually, but cannot overturn the paper-level decision established by S1-S3.

one_line_finding: Advice following LLM learning was more similar across writers than advice following web-link learning (cosine similarity 0.159 vs 0.057, 0.224 vs 0.072, and 0.214 vs 0.073 in Experiments 1-3; all P < 0.001; pp. 5-7) and was rated less helpful by recipients (3.553 vs 3.816; P < 0.001; p. 8).

notes: Finalization read all 398 lines of the markdown conversion through the references and independently extracted and checked all 11 saved PDF pages with PyMuPDF. The saved PDF has no supplementary appendix or embedded files. All populated study counts, demographics, procedure numbers, durations, output means, test statistics, P values, and choice percentages were checked against their PDF passages. No effect size, missing count, SD, or SE was computed. There are 15 retained outcome entries: 13 output-scored entries and two ancillary recipient intentions (S3-O7 and S3-O8), which are self_report, scored_on_output=false, and question=none. Levenshtein checks remain variants of the three diversity outcomes, and relative helpfulness choice remains a variant of the helpfulness rating. Main-text measures are retained; supplementary outcomes could not be exhaustively screened. Writers' self-reported learning, effort and ownership, time on task, recipient topic relevance, and mediation-path coefficients are not separate creative-output outcomes. Six raw-count measure codes are null because neither LIWC word count nor spaCy factual-entity count is a creativity-scoring model under the current codebook. Their operation, construct, and printed results are retained. No outcome SD or SE is supplied for the main-text contrasts; supplement precision is unknown. Diversity analysis rows and dependence adjustments are not established by the PDF. The paper-wide totals disagree (10,462 in the abstract, p. 1; 10,426 in the introduction, p. 2), so eligibility uses the directly stated analyzed writer counts. The contradictory helpfulness-choice labels on p. 8 remain as printed, with direction null. AI access during writing remains unconfirmed, so question and availability fields for the output-scored measures stay null. The Experiment 4 evaluations remain attached to the Experiment 3 writer sample and its lab_rct design; S4 records only the separate analyzed recipient sample and measurement procedure. No additional AI-assigned writer sample is inferred. OSF is named on p. 10 but no repository or code URL is supplied in the text or PDF link annotations. Finalization attempts to retrieve supplementary content via Europe PMC and the PMC Open Access API failed with WinError 10013. The reconciliation object is preserved unchanged as an earlier audit snapshot; final.challenge_resolution records all eight subsequent corrections. In final.open_items, affects_eligibility identifies an unresolved criterion for the named study, including supplementary studies. Those study-specific questions do not overturn paper-level core=yes, established independently by S1-S3.
